<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915265_theRebbe_887" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915265_theRebbe_887__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the opening header and date of the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">Shabbos Parshas Vayeitzei,</t>
    <t s="2">the 9th of Kislev,</t>
    <t s="3">the year 5729</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section questions why the verse uses the term "one" (echad) rather than "singular" (yachid) for Hashem and Israel.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"You are One"</t>
    <t s="1">"and Your Name is One, and who is like Your people Israel,"</t>
    <t s="2">"a unique nation on earth."</t>
    <t s="3">And my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, precisely analyzes in his maamar beginning with the words "Zeh" of the 9th of Kislev,</t>
    <t s="4">that the term "one" (echad) also refers to a numerical one,</t>
    <t s="5">[as in "And there was evening and there was morning, one day,"</t>
    <t s="6">and afterwards</t>
    <t s="7">it is written "a second day," "a third day," etc.],</t>
    <t s="8">and since He, blessed be He, is singular and unique, with nothing comparable to Him, and similarly Israel is a unique nation, singular and unparalleled,</t>
    <t s="9">it should have said "You are Singular (Yachid) and Your Name is Singular, and who is like Your people Israel, a singular nation."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Israel being a "unique nation" is analogous to an only child, whose love is greater, and questions why the verse says "one nation" rather than "singular nation."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And he continues in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="1">that this—that Israel is a singular nation—is analogous to a father and mother who have only one son, who is called an only son.</t>
    <t s="2">For the love of parents for their son, when they have only an only son, is a greater love than the love of parents for their children when they have additional children.</t>
    <t s="3">And likewise, the love of an only son for his parents is greater than when there is more than one son.</t>
    <t s="4">And so it is also with Israel,</t>
    <t s="5">since Israel is an only son to the Singular One of the world,</t>
    <t s="6">therefore,</t>
    <t s="7">the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel,</t>
    <t s="8">and likewise the love of Israel for the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="9">is an exceedingly great love.</t>
    <t s="10">And he concludes there,</t>
    <t s="11">that based on this, one must understand why it is said "and who is like Your people Israel, a unique nation (goy echad)" and not "a singular nation (goy yachid)."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
